label: Game A
nuance_found: Auto-fire only locks on ink, so you must aim at attackers yourself or they chew you up; Bloom charged by kills paints colour back and a wave must be cleared before the inkwell opens. I only partly found this and mostly never saw what was killing me.
audio: A looping music bed from the first tap, plus repeated same-sounding zap and noise effects when firing; nothing that felt like a reward.
furthest_progress: Still on the first objective (Break the inkwell in the Olive Terraces, 'Nodes open' reached once after clearing a wave), score 45,231, 1.4% restored, died many times.
control_trouble: Aiming with the right thumb is coarse for me, and I could not see attackers while turning, so some of the deaths are my clumsiness; the screen rotated into ground or sky views from big drags.
best_moment: Bloom burst turning grey ground into golden grass and red poppies with VIVID x2 popping up.
worst_moment: Being drained by pink damage arcs from things I could not see, dying with zero kills in the first minute, then losing a tenth of my score each time.
verdict: Gorgeous to look at, the painted grey world blooming into colour is a real hook. But the first minute was brutal: I died with no kills and no idea what hit me, and the first message told me to walk to a gold mark I could not find. Once I stopped walking and learned Bloom, it got better, yet the fire button gives almost no sight of hits, so it feels like luck. I would give it a second go if a friend said it gets good, but I would not seek it out.
